notes.path: e4 c6
notes.text: The Caro-Kann. 1...c6 prepares ...d5 to challenge White's centre. The light-squared bishop comes out to f5 or g4 before ...e6, so it never gets shut in. Black aims for a solid position, not a quick fight.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5
notes.text: Now the e4 pawn is attacked. White must choose: push it to e5, exchange on d5, or defend it with Nc3.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5
notes.text: The Advance Variation. Get the bishop out before ...e6 closes its diagonal. Then ...e6, ...c5 and ...Nc6 attack White's pawn chain from the front.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6
notes.text: Solid: ...e6 supports d5 and frees the dark-squared bishop. Next come ...c5 to hit d4, and the knights to d7 and e7.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Bd3 Bxd3
notes.text: Trade the bishops. White offers the trade, and without its light-squared bishop White has one attacker less.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 e6
notes.text: Now ...e6 costs nothing, since the bishop is already out and traded. Black plays ...c5 and ...Nc6 against d4.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 e6 Nf3 c5
notes.text: 6...c5 hits d4, the base of White's pawn chain. The queen and knights will add pressure on d4.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5
notes.text: The Exchange Variation. Taking with the c-pawn keeps a pawn in the centre and opens the c-file for Black's rook. The position is calm and equal.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Nf3 Nc6
notes.text: Develop and put pressure on d4. Next ...Bg4 pins the knight that defends it.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bg4
notes.text: Pin the knight on f3, so d4 has one defender less. Black develops easily and stands well.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Bg4
notes.text: The same idea: ...Bg4 pins the knight and adds pressure on d4.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6
notes.text: Against Bd3, develop and hit d4. ...Nf6 and ...Bg4 come next.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Nc3 Nf6
notes.text: Develop and guard d5. ...Bg4 or ...Nc6 follow.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Bg4
notes.text: Pin the knight and keep an eye on d4. The bishop is outside the pawn chain, where it belongs in the Caro-Kann.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4
notes.text: Take on e4. White's knight recaptures, and Black gains time by attacking it. This is the Classical Caro-Kann.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5
notes.text: Develop with a threat: the bishop attacks the knight on e4. Black follows with ...e6, ...Nd7 and ...Ngf6.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6
notes.text: Keep the bishop: it drops back to g6 and still watches the long diagonal. If White plays h4 to chase it, ...h6 gives it room.

notes.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 Nf3 Nd7
notes.text: 6...Nd7 stops Ne5, which would hit the bishop on g6. Then ...Ngf6 and ...e6 finish development.

notes.path: e4 c6 Nf3 d5
notes.text: Against 2.Nf3, play ...d5 anyway: e4 is attacked and White must decide what to do with it.

notes.path: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 exd5 cxd5
notes.text: Recapture with the c-pawn and keep a pawn in the centre. After d4, develop with ...Nf6 and ...Nc6, as in the Exchange Variation.

notes.path: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 e5 Bg4
notes.text: With the knight on f3, ...Bg4 pins it and gets the bishop out before ...e6. Then ...e6, ...c5 and ...Nc6.

notes.path: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 e5 Bg4 d4 e6
notes.text: Now ...e6 is safe, because the bishop is already outside the chain. Next is ...c5 to attack d4.

notes.path: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 Nc3 dxe4
notes.text: Take on e4. The knight recaptures, and Black develops with ...Nf6, hitting it.

notes.path: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6
notes.text: Challenge the knight on e4. If White trades, Black's pieces come out easily.

notes.path: e4 c6 Nc3 d5
notes.text: Against 2.Nc3 the plan is the same: ...d5 attacks e4. After 3.d4 dxe4 it is the Classical again.

notes.path: e4 c6 Nc3 d5 exd5 cxd5
notes.text: Keep a pawn in the centre. ...Nf6 and ...Nc6 follow.

notes.path: e4 c6 Bc4 d5
notes.text: 2.Bc4 runs into ...d5, which hits the bishop and the e4 pawn at once. White has nothing better than taking on d5.

notes.path: e4 c6 Bc4 d5 exd5 cxd5
notes.text: Recapture, and the bishop on c4 is attacked again. Black has the centre and an easy game.

notes.path: e4 c6 Bc4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bb3 Nf6
notes.text: Develop. White's bishop on b3 only hits the solid pawn on d5. ...Nc6 and ...e6 or ...Bf5 follow.

notes.path: e4 c6 f4 d5
notes.text: Against 2.f4 the answer is the same ...d5. The pawn on f4 does not defend e4, and it loosens White's king.
